LESSON: READING 3.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: REFERENCE MATERIALS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.1 Extensive reading: Reference materials
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 3.2.1 Extensive reading: Reference materials, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why are reference materials useful? 2.Why should one read extensively?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

A. explain the uses of reference materials (dictionary, thesaurus, atlases, manuals, newspapers and an encyclopedi

   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

1. work with peers to look for information online and offline on the uses of the dictionary, thesaurus, atlases, manuals, newspaper cuttings and the encyclopedia. 2. collaboratively locate synonyms and antonyms in a thesaurus,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to look for information online and offline on the uses of the dictionary, thesaurus, atlases, manuals, newspaper cuttings and the encyclopedia. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted,
2. collaboratively locate synonyms and antonyms in a thesaurus,
3. use a dictionary to find the spelling, meaning and articulation of words. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 3.2.1 Extensive reading: Reference materials together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy as the learner downloads reference materials and writes down examples of such materials used in

extensive reading.

● Citizenship as the learner engages effectively with peers as they locate synonyms and antonyms in a thesaurus.

Values:
● Love is nurtured as the learner shows care and concern for peers when they share resources to pick out information

from atlases, manuals, newspapers and encyclopedia.

45

● Peace is promoted as the learner displays tolerance as they work with peers to locate synonyms and antonyms in a

thesaurus.

Pertinent contemporary issues (PCIs):

Life skills as learners enhance a developmental perspective when they use a dictionary to find spelling, meaning and

articulation of words.

Suggested Learning Resources: Dictionaries, charts, digital devices, audio visuals, internet, realia, adapted digital

devices with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand. universal cuffs/wrist

braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips
